results.content: Clinical characteristics and outcomes of incidental venous thromboembolism in cancer patients: Insights from the Caravaggio study - ScienceDirect Skip to main contentSkip to article Cumulative incidence of (A) recurrent venous thromboembolism (VTE) and (B)… Journal of Thrombosis and Haemostasis Volume 19, Issue 11, November 2021, Pages 2751-2759 Clinical characteristics and outcomes of incidental venous thromboembolism in cancer patients: Insights from the Caravaggio study Author links open overlay panel Michela Giustozzi 1, Jean M.Connors 2, Ana Belen Ruperez Blanco 3, Sebastian Szmit 4, Nicolas Falvo 5, Alexander T.Cohen 6, Menno Huisman 7, Rupert Bauersachs 8, Francesco Dentali 9, Cecilia Becattini 1, Giancarlo Agnelli 1 Under a Creative Commons license ### Background Clinical guidelines advise similar anticoagulant treatment for symptomatic and incidental cancer‐associated venous thromboembolism (VTE). In this study, the following main observations were made: (1) PE with or without DVT as index event, colorectal cancer, ECOG score of 0, and locally advanced or metastatic cancer were more frequent in patients with incidental VTE while DVT, hematological cancer, and ECOG score of 2 were more frequent in patients with symptomatic VTE; (2) despite anticoagulation, cancer patients with incidental VTE have a considerable rate of recurrent VTE; the 6‐month risk of recurrent VTE is numerically lower compared to patients with symptomatic VTE; (3) the 6‐month risk of major bleeding is numerically higher in patients with incidental VTE compared to those with symptomatic VTE, although not statistically significantly different; (4) the rates for recurrence and major bleeding associated with apixaban and dalteparin were consistent in patients with symptomatic and incidental cancer‐associated VTE. * ### Performance Status and Long-Term Outcomes in Cancer-Associated Pulmonary Embolism: Insights From the Hokusai-VTE Cancer Study 2022, Jacc Cardiooncology Citation Excerpt : In a previous analysis of the overall VTE population of the Hokusai-VTE Cancer trial, there was no statistical difference in terms of the primary outcome.27 However, a recent predefined analysis of the Caravaggio trial showed that statistically significant lower risk for recurrent VTE and no difference in risk for major bleeding in patients with incidental compared with symptomatic VTE.28 The present analysis included a diverse population of patients with cancer with extended baseline high-quality data, minimal rates of loss to follow-up, and adjudication of all events by an independent blinded committee.

results.title: Best Practices for Clinical Endpoint Adjudication in Decentralized Trials: Insights from ICH E6(R3) Annex 2
results.content: Home / Endpoint Adjudication Blog / Best Practices for Clinical Endpoint Adjudication in Decentralized Trials: Insights from ICH E6(R3) Annex 2 # Best Practices for Clinical Endpoint Adjudication in Decentralized Trials: Insights from ICH E6(R3) Annex 2 To ensure consistency, accuracy, and regulatory compliance in endpoint adjudication within DCTs, sponsors and investigators must adopt **best practices** in three key areas: **pre-specified adjudication criteria, centralized blinded adjudication, and robust data validation processes**. * **Protocol-Level Adjudication Criteria**: The clinical trial protocol should **clearly define the endpoints** and specify how adjudicators will handle decentralized data sources such as patient-reported outcomes (PROs) and remote imaging. A **robust data validation framework** ensures that clinical endpoint adjudication in decentralized trials meets **regulatory expectations** while maintaining scientific rigor and patient safety.

results.title: Hemostatic and thrombotic disorders in the pediatric patient
results.content: We will describe the development of validated bleeding assessment tools relevant to pediatric practice, laboratory advances in the evaluation of von Willebrand disease, and a shift in clinical practice regarding the interpretation of normal coagulation studies in patients with significant bleeding phenotypes. The EINSTEIN-Jr CVC-VTE, a predefined substudy of EINSTEIN-Jr, investigated the VTE risk factor profile of 126 pediatric patients with symptomatic or asymptomatic CVC-VTE who received either rivaroxaban (n = 90) or standard AC (n = 36).51 Anticoagulant therapy with either rivaroxaban or standard AC in children after initial heparin therapy was efficacious (no recurrence), safe (no major bleeding), and associated with complete or partial vein recanalization in more than 90% of the 103 evaluable children. Two VTE outcomes, PTS and post-PE syndrome, have gained recent increased attention,64 because of their impact on the quality of life.65,66 A systematic review of the frequency of pediatric PTS after lower or upper extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) reported an overall frequency of 26% and a frequency of 17% when only considering prospective studies.64 In a recent systematic review of 12 studies involving 1076 patients, CVC‐associated DVT, complete veno‐occlusion, and incomplete DVT resolution were deemed as statistically significant prognostic factors for the development of pediatric PTS.67 There are several instruments to measure PTS and no accepted gold standard.68 The Modified Villalta Scale and the Manco-Johnson Instrument are the current reference instruments proposed by the ISTH for the “definition and outcome measurement” of PTS in children,69 but only the Manco-Johnson Instrument has undergone both reliability and validity testing.70 Their use for the definition and outcome assessment of upper extremity PTS was acknowledged but not explicitly endorsed by the ISTH.71 One study compared 2 pediatric PTS instruments (the Modified Villalta Scale and Manco-Johnson Instrument) to each other, as well as to the validated, widely accepted adult Villalta scale in a group of older children and young adolescents with DVT and showed significant discordance between the prevalence of PTS.68 These instruments represent a step toward a more consistent definition of pediatric PTS but do not capture the full clinical impact of PTS and overdiagnose mild PTS.

results.content: Endpoint Adjudication Open/Close sub menu. # Streamlining Endpoint Adjudication: Tips and Tools. ## Streamlining endpoint adjudication has a significant impact on the success of clinical trials. By focusing on regulatory compliance, building effective adjudication committees, and optimizing workflows through the use of advanced technologies, clinical trial managers can boost the reliability and efficiency of data collection and analysis processes. Endpoint adjudication plays a crucial role in clinical trials, ensuring study results solidity. As the complexity of clinical trials continues to grow, streamlining the adjudication process has become essential to enhance efficiency and accuracy while maintaining regulatory compliance. This article explores key strategies to optimize endpoint adjudication in clinical trials. Regulatory Considerations in Endpoint Adjudication. Endpoint adjudication in clinical trials is subject to stringent regulatory oversight to ensure data integrity and consistency. Image-based endpoints are frequently adjudicated to remove subjective bias and these standards help maintain data quality across trial sites and create a verifiable record of the imaging process. Globally, central adjudication of endpoints is considered the gold standard in clinical trials. Clinical Adjudication Committees (CACs) play a crucial role in standardizing endpoint reviews and reducing bias in clinical trials. Committee members independently adjudicate complex clinical events in a blinded and timely manner. Streamlining the endpoint adjudication process involves implementing efficient strategies to enhance data management, collaboration, and task automation. By leveraging advanced technologies and optimizing workflows, organizations can significantly improve the speed and accuracy of endpoint adjudication while maintaining regulatory compliance. By focusing on regulatory compliance, building effective endpoint adjudication committees, and optimizing workflows, clinical trial managers can expect more robust and trustworthy clinical trial results. The use of advanced technologies supports streamlined adjudication processes and is crucial to enhance the speed and accuracy of endpoint adjudication. Implementing a reliable clinical endpoint adjudication software like eAdjudication® can greatly improve the overall efficiency of the adjudication workflow. results.title: The power of clinical adjudication | Clario
results.content: 1. Home Resources Blog Articles The power of clinical adjudication. # The power of clinical adjudication. Clinical trials are essential for medical advancements, ensuring treatments are safe and effective before reaching patients. Clinical adjudication addresses these challenges by introducing an independent, standardized review process, improving data reliability and regulatory confidence. ## What is clinical adjudication and why does it matter? Clinical adjudication is a structured process in which an independent committee of medical experts reviews trial events with predefined criteria to determine a positive or negative outcome. Unlike investigator-reported outcomes, which can be subject to bias, adjudication committees apply consistent, blinded evaluation of source data to ensure greater accuracy and reliability. By implementing an independent adjudication process, trial results become more credible and adds another level of confidence. Regulatory agencies such as the FDA and EMA increasingly recommend adjudication for primary safety and efficacy outcomes, recognizing its role in producing robust, accurate data. Trials that lack adjudication can face endpoint disputes, delays in regulatory review, and even the risk of failure due to inconsistent data. ## How clinical adjudication enhances trial outcomes. Adjudication improves regulatory confidence by ensuring data undergoes a structured, blinded review, making it more reliable than investigator-assessed outcomes. Additionally, adjudication reduces discrepancies in endpoint classifications across study sites, strengthening data integrity and minimizing delays. By minimizing disputes over endpoint classification, adjudication also enhances efficiency. Early adjudication integration helps prevent inefficiencies, streamlining regulatory submissions. ## Key strategies for effective adjudication. Adjudicators and study site personnel must be well-versed in workflows to maintain consistency. Partnering with experienced adjudication providers can help maintain consistency and regulatory compliance across single or multi-study programs. ## Why sponsors should prioritize adjudication. In today’s regulatory landscape, clinical adjudication is not just an option—it’s a necessity for trials with complex and subjective endpoints. By implementing adjudication early in the trial design, sponsors can improve data accuracy, minimize bias, reduce endpoint disputes, and accelerate the approval process. As agencies continue to emphasize the importance of objective, standardized data, adjudication will only become more critical in ensuring clinical trial success. A well-executed adjudication process can ultimately enable faster approvals and a clearer path for sponsors to bring innovative treatments to market.
